conclusion: The current benchmark stack can measure WooCommerce core plus Stripe, PayPal Payments, and WooPayments bootstrap/admin/cart behavior, but it cannot truthfully benchmark WooCommerce Subscriptions renewal flows or WooCommerce Bookings checkout/calendar flows because the commercial Subscriptions and Bookings extensions are not installed or loaded. Static code in the active gateway plugins identifies the next hot paths to profile once a licensed fixture is available.

runtime_environment.server: wordpress:php8.3-apache container on Docker Compose, MySQL 8.0 container

subscription_hot_paths_to_profile_with_f.area: WooCommerce source Subscriptions engine renewal path
static_path: one Action Scheduler row per primitive-scheduled contract
ContractRepository::find hydrates row, items, addresses, and meta
renewal_exists_for_cycle uses unbounded wc_get_orders by contract meta
build_renewal_order writes a Woo order and recurring line items
resolve_outcome updates cycle and contract schedule fields
subscription_hot_paths_to_profile_with_f.why_it_is_interesting: This is the package-level renewal money path in the WooCommerce source tree. It combines Action Scheduler scale, custom subscription tables, HPOS/order writes, order item writes, and gateway hooks.

static_path: get subscription by WCPay subscription ID
subscription_hot_paths_to_profile_with_f.why_it_is_interesting: This combines subscription lookup, HPOS meta-query order lookup by invoice ID, renewal order creation, payment completion side effects, and remote invoice/charge metadata updates.

static_path: subscription lookup by WCPay subscription ID
subscription_hot_paths_to_profile_with_f.why_it_is_interesting: Failure handling can combine remote charge retrieval, renewal order creation, notes/meta writes, and subscription status changes in one webhook request.

subscription_hot_paths_to_profile_with_f.area: WooPayments subscription migration Action Scheduler flow
static_path: validate Subscriptions extension and subscription state
subscription_hot_paths_to_profile_with_f.why_it_is_interesting: This is a background batch lane likely to surface Action Scheduler throughput, remote API latency, repeated subscription object saves, and meta/order-note write amplification.

static_path: scheduled_subscription_payment forwards renewal order to process_subscription_payment
failed payment method update and change-payment-method hooks also attach
wcs_get_subscriptions_for_renewal_order used in payment intent/mandate paths
subscription_hot_paths_to_profile_with_f.why_it_is_interesting: The renewal path crosses gateway API calls, renewal order processing, subscription lookup, failed-payment handling, and mandate/payment-method metadata.
A customer with many active subscriptions can turn one add-payment-method request into a loop over subscription objects and payment-method writes.

static_path: failed order status update on exception
subscription_hot_paths_to_profile_with_f.why_it_is_interesting: The handler combines renewal-order subscription lookup, related-order scans for previous transactions, saved-payment-token lookup, PayPal API calls, and order status writes.
This is a focused write path for subscription payment-method changes and should be profiled with users that have many tokens/subscriptions.

booking_hot_paths_to_profile_with_fixtur.why_it_is_interesting: The existing gateway profile found WooPayments multicurrency can add tens of thousands of calls on large variation pages. Booking cost/resource/person filters may produce a similar multiplier on calendar cost calculation and add-to-cart flows.

static_path: WC_Cart::add_to_cart with booking cart item data
booking_hot_paths_to_profile_with_fixtur.why_it_is_interesting: This is the gateway button path for booking products and should be profiled against bookable products with resources, persons, availability rules, and blocked ranges.

static_path: Bookings compatibility assets and integration setup
booking_hot_paths_to_profile_with_fixtur.why_it_is_interesting: The module is dormant in the current stack. With Bookings active, it should be included in checkout/button/calendar profiles so compatibility boot cost is separated from core booking cost calculation.
